CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog tool
The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog is a CISA list of security flaws known to have been exploited.
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog organization
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog is a U.S. government list of security flaws that attackers are known to be using in the real world.
also: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
Citizen Lab organization
Citizen Lab is a research group at the University of Toronto known for investigating spyware, censorship, and digital threats.
Claroty organization
A cybersecurity company that researches and protects industrial and operational technology systems.
Classified concept
Classified information is government information restricted because releasing it could harm national security or other protected interests.
claude
Claude is Anthropic’s family of AI assistants and language models.
also: Claude research model
Claude agents product
AI systems based on Claude that can carry out multi-step tasks using tools and instructions.
claude-code
Claude Code is Anthropic’s AI coding assistant for helping developers write and manage software projects.
cleartext concept
Cleartext is data that is readable as-is because it is not encrypted.
Client-side concept
Client-side refers to code or activity that runs on a user’s device or browser rather than on a server.
Client-Side Code concept
Website or application code that runs on a user's device or browser and can usually be inspected by visitors.
Client-side JavaScript concept
Code written in JavaScript that runs in a visitor's web browser rather than on the website's server.
also: client-side collection code, JavaScript
Clop threat-actor
Clop is a ransomware group and malware family known for stealing data and extorting victims.
also: Clop ransomware gang, the ransomware gang
cloud concept
The cloud is internet-based computing where data and applications run on remote servers instead of only on your own device.
Cloud Access Keys concept
Secret credentials that allow software or people to access cloud accounts and services.
cloud account concept
A cloud account is an account used to access and manage computing resources such as servers, storage, and databases from a cloud provider.
Cloud credentials concept
Cloud credentials are passwords, keys, or tokens used to access cloud services and resources.
cloud infrastructure concept
Cloud infrastructure is computing infrastructure provided through internet-based services.
cloud provider concept
A cloud provider is a company that offers computing services such as servers, storage, and databases over the internet.
cloud resources concept
Cloud resources are computing services like servers, storage, databases, or apps that run in an internet-hosted cloud environment.
cloud secrets concept
Sensitive values, such as passwords, API keys, or tokens, that allow access to cloud services.
Cloud security concept
Cloud security means protecting data, applications, and accounts that run in cloud services.
cloud services concept
Computing resources—like storage, apps, and networking—delivered over the internet by providers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program organization
Google's program that pays researchers for reporting eligible security vulnerabilities in Google Cloud.
cloud-hosted concept
Stored or run on internet-connected provider infrastructure instead of directly on a local device.
cloudflare
Cloudflare is a company that provides content delivery, DDoS protection, DNS, and web security services.
Cloudflare Bot Management product
Cloudflare Bot Management is a Cloudflare product that detects and controls automated bot traffic to websites.
Cloudflare Radar product
Cloudflare Radar is a public service from Cloudflare that shows internet traffic trends, outages, and security activity.
also: Radar
Cloudflare Turnstile product
A user-friendly CAPTCHA alternative by Cloudflare that verifies humans without puzzles, preserving privacy.
also: Turnstile
Cloudflare WAF product
Cloudflare WAF is Cloudflare's web application firewall that helps block malicious web traffic before it reaches a website.
cluster concept
A group of connected computers or appliances that work together as one system.
Clusters concept
Clusters are groups of connected computers or nodes that work together as one system.
CMD product
The Windows Command Prompt, a text-based interface where users type commands to run programs and system tasks.
cobalt-strike
Cobalt Strike is a legitimate penetration-testing tool that attackers often abuse to control compromised systems.
also: Cobalt Strike framework, Cobalt Strike server
code execution technique
Code execution means an attacker can make a computer or server run commands or software of their choosing.
Code repositories concept
Code repositories are storage locations where software source code and its change history are kept.
code repository tool
A code repository is an online or local storage place where software source code and its change history are kept.
Codebases concept
Codebases are the collections of source code that make up an application, service, or software project.
codex
Codex is an OpenAI AI coding model or coding assistant technology for helping write and understand code.
codex-x product
An AI coding package or service referenced in security reporting.
coding concept
Coding is writing instructions in a programming language so a computer can perform tasks.
Coercion concept
Coercion is forcing or pressuring someone to do something against their will, sometimes used in scams or extortion.
also: Protecting voters against coercion
Comet product
Comet is a named product, tool, or threat component referenced in security reporting.
Command and control domains concept
Command and control domains are internet addresses malware uses to receive instructions from its operators.
also: domains the botnet was communicating with, domains used to control the botnet
command execution technique
Command execution means making a computer or device run instructions, often through a shell or remote interface.
command injection technique
Command injection is an attack where someone tricks an application into running system commands chosen by the attacker.
command injection flaw vulnerability
A security flaw that lets an attacker execute arbitrary commands on the host operating system through a vulnerable application.
command injection vulnerability vulnerability
A command injection vulnerability lets an attacker sneak operating-system commands into an application so the server runs them.
Command Line concept
A text-based way to control a computer by typing commands instead of clicking buttons.
Command-and-control server concept
Remote computers controlled by attackers that send orders to infected devices and collect stolen data.
commercial surveillance tools tool
Commercial surveillance tools are privately sold technologies used to monitor people, devices, or communications, sometimes controversially by governments or investigators.
commit concept
A saved set of changes in a version-control system such as Git.
commit SHA concept
A commit SHA is the unique identifier for a specific code change in a Git repository.
Commitment technique
A cryptographic value that locks in information for later verification without revealing the information itself.
also: ballot commitments, committed ciphertext
commits concept
Commits are saved sets of changes to files in a source-code repository.
Common Access Card product
A smart identification card used by United States military personnel and certain government workers.
communication patterns concept
Communication patterns are the regular ways systems, users, or malware send and receive data, which can help identify normal or suspicious behavior.
Compensating controls concept
Alternative security measures used to reduce risk when a preferred control cannot be put in place.
also: compensating control
Complete control concept
Complete control means an attacker can fully manage a system, account, or application as if they owned it.
Composer tool
Composer is a dependency manager that helps PHP projects download and manage the libraries they need.
composer require tool
composer require is a Composer command that adds a new PHP dependency to a project.
composer update tool
composer update is a Composer command that refreshes a PHP project’s dependencies to allowed newer versions.
composer.json product
composer.json is the main configuration file that lists a PHP project’s dependencies and Composer settings.
compromise concept
A compromise is a situation where a system, account, or data has been breached or taken over by an attacker.
compromised concept
Compromised means a system, account, or device has been accessed or controlled by someone who should not have access.
compromised account concept
An account whose credentials have been stolen or guessed, allowing an attacker to impersonate the legitimate user.
compromised build concept
A compromised build is software that was tampered with during the build process before users received it.
compromised computers concept
Compromised computers are devices that attackers have gained unauthorized access to or control over.
compromised credentials concept
Compromised credentials are login details that have been stolen, exposed, or otherwise made unsafe.
Compromised devices concept
Compromised devices are computers, phones, or systems that attackers have gained unauthorized control over.
Compromised server concept
A compromised server is a computer system that an attacker has broken into or taken control of.
Compromised systems concept
Compromised systems are computers, servers, or devices that an attacker has successfully broken into or controlled.
Confidence concept
Confidence is a measure of how certain a security team is that an alert or finding is truly malicious.
configuration files concept
Configuration files are files that store settings telling software or systems how to behave.
connected devices concept
Connected devices are everyday or business devices that can communicate over a network or the internet, such as phones, cameras, sensors, or appliances.
Connected Network Drives concept
Storage locations on another computer or server that appear as drives on a user's computer.
Connected Refrigeration Controllers product
Connected refrigeration controllers are networked devices that manage the temperature and operation of refrigeration equipment.
Connecting concept
Connecting is a status meaning a device, app, or service is trying to establish a network connection.
consumer ISP organization
A consumer ISP is a company that provides internet service to homes and individual customers.
Contact Details concept
Information used to contact a person, such as an address, email address, or phone number.
Contagious Interview technique
Contagious Interview is a North Korea-linked campaign that tricks job seekers or developers into running malicious software during fake interviews.
container concept
A container is a lightweight package that runs an application with its needed files in an isolated environment.
container deployment token concept
A secret credential that allows software to deploy or manage applications packaged in containers.
containers concept
Containers are lightweight packages that run applications with their needed files in isolated environments.
also: containers on the same host
containment technique
Containment is the process of limiting a cyber incident so attackers or malware cannot spread further.
Context-Reframing technique
A prompt technique that changes how a request is described in an attempt to bypass AI safety rules.
conti
Conti was a major ransomware group known for attacking organizations and leaking stolen data.
continuous concept
In security, continuous means something is monitored or updated all the time instead of only during occasional checks.
Continuous Exposure Management concept
Continuous Exposure Management is the ongoing process of finding, prioritizing, and fixing security weaknesses before attackers use them.
Continuous Threat Exposure Management concept
Continuous Threat Exposure Management is an ongoing security approach for finding, prioritizing, and reducing weaknesses attackers could use.
Contractors concept
Contractors are outside workers or companies hired to perform work for another organization.
Control Networks concept
Networks used to operate industrial equipment, building systems, or other physical processes.
Controller concept
A controller is a component that manages or directs how other parts of a system behave.
controllers concept
System components that manage or direct how other parts of an application or infrastructure behave.
cookies concept
Cookies are small pieces of data websites store in a browser to remember logins, settings, or tracking information.
cooldown concept
A cooldown is a waiting period before something can happen again.
Coop organization
A consumer cooperative retail organization and supermarket brand.
Copeland organization
Copeland is a company that makes refrigeration, heating, and cooling equipment and controls.
corporate networks concept
Corporate networks are the connected computers, servers, and systems used by a company.
also: corporate systems
cPanel product
cPanel is a popular web hosting control panel used to manage websites, email, files, and server settings.
cPGuard product
A security product for Linux web servers that provides malware detection and other protective features.
also: cPGuard web security suite, cPGuard servers
credential files concept
Credential files are files that store login secrets such as passwords, API keys, tokens, or certificates.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-based authentication concept
A login method in which a user proves their identity with credentials such as a username and password.
credential-dumping technique
Credential-dumping is stealing stored usernames, passwords, or login tokens from a computer or system.
also: extract and decrypt credentials, memory-dumping
Credential-Harvesting Payload malware
Malicious code designed to collect usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login secrets.
credential-stealing technique
Credential-stealing is the act of stealing login details such as passwords, session cookies, or access tokens.
credential-stuffing technique
Credential stuffing is when attackers try stolen usernames and passwords on many websites to see where they still work.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
also: login details
Crime-as-a-service concept
A criminal business model where cybercriminals sell or rent tools, data, or services that help others commit crimes online.
criminal affiliates threat-actor
Outside criminals who work with or buy services from a larger cybercrime operation.
also: cybercriminals
critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.
Critical services concept
Critical services are essential systems or functions whose failure would seriously harm operations or public services.
critical systems concept
Critical systems are important systems whose failure could seriously affect operations or safety.
critical vulnerabilities vulnerability
Critical vulnerabilities are very serious security flaws that could let attackers cause major damage or gain major access.
Critical vulnerability vulnerability
A critical vulnerability is a very serious security flaw that can cause major damage if exploited.
CRM systems product
Customer relationship management systems are business tools used to store customer details and track sales or support interactions.
also: CRM
Cross-Service Logic Flaws vulnerability
Security weaknesses caused by unsafe interactions between separate online services or features.
crowdstrike organization
CrowdStrike is a cybersecurity company known for endpoint protection, threat intelligence, and incident response.
CryptoBilis organization
A reseller organization that sells cryptocurrency hardware products.
cryptocurrency concept
Cryptocurrency is digital money, such as Bitcoin, that uses cryptography and usually runs on a blockchain.
Cryptocurrency exchange concept
An online service where people can buy, sell, trade, or store digital currencies.
also: exchange
cryptocurrency payments concept
Cryptocurrency payments are transfers of digital currency such as Bitcoin or Ethereum instead of traditional money.
cryptocurrency thefts concept
Cryptocurrency thefts are crimes where attackers steal digital currencies such as Bitcoin or Ethereum.
Cryptocurrency Transfers concept
Cryptocurrency transfers are movements of digital money such as Bitcoin or Ethereum between online wallets.
cryptocurrency wallet product
A cryptocurrency wallet is software or hardware used to store and use the keys that control digital coins.
Cryptographic Identity concept
A digital identity established with cryptographic keys so a person or system can securely prove who they are.
also: digital cryptographic identity
cryptographic systems concept
Cryptographic systems are tools and methods that protect information using encryption, signatures, and related math.
Cryptographically Prove Unauthorized Access technique
A safe method of using cryptography to demonstrate that unauthorized access is possible without harming real systems.
Cryptography concept
Cryptography is the use of mathematical methods to protect information from being read or changed by unauthorized people.
also: cryptographic techniques
cryptojacking technique
Cryptojacking is when attackers secretly use someone else’s computer power to mine cryptocurrency.
CryptoPayment Gateway product
A WordPress plugin that adds cryptocurrency payment-processing features to a website.
CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin product
A WordPress add-on that enables a website to accept cryptocurrency payments.
CSRF technique
CSRF is a web attack where a site is tricked into performing an action using a logged-in user's session without the user's intent.
also: CORS/CSRF chain, CORS/CSRF variant
CSV concept
CSV can mean comma-separated values, a simple spreadsheet-like file format, or cluster shared volumes in Windows clustering depending on context.
also: Comma-Separated Values
curl
curl is a command-line tool used to transfer data to or from servers using protocols like HTTP and HTTPS.
cursor
Cursor is an AI-assisted code editor built for software developers.
Custom code concept
Software code written or changed specifically for an organization's own needs.
custom malware malware
Custom malware is malicious software specially built or modified for a particular attacker, target, or campaign.
Customer accounts concept
Customer accounts are user records and logins that let customers access a company's services.
Customer Names concept
Names that identify customers and may be sensitive when exposed in a data breach.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVE records concept
CVE records are public entries that identify and describe known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS concept
CVSS is a standard scoring system used to rate how severe a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS scale
CVSS 10.0 concept
CVSS 10.0 is the highest severity score on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System scale for rating security flaws.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
also: CVSS score of 10.0
CVSS score of 9.8 concept
A very high rating on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, indicating a critical security flaw.
CVSS Scores concept
Standard numerical ratings used to describe the technical severity of software vulnerabilities.
CVSS severity scores concept
Standardized numerical ratings used to estimate how severe a known software vulnerability is.
cyber attack concept
A cyber attack is an attempt to break into, disrupt, steal from, or damage computers, accounts, networks, or data.
also: digital break-in
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
also: hacks
cyber operations concept
Activities conducted in cyberspace including espionage, sabotage, or defense, typically by state-sponsored groups.
cyber risk concept
Cyber risk is the chance that digital systems, data, or operations could be harmed by security problems.
Cyber Security and Resilience Bill concept
The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is proposed UK legislation intended to strengthen cybersecurity rules and incident reporting.
Cyber Shield product
Cyber Shield is a cybersecurity-related named program, product, or operation referenced in security reporting.
cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
cybercrime concept
Cybercrime is crime carried out using computers, networks, or the internet.
Cybercrime Actor threat-actor
A person or group that carries out crimes using computers, networks, or online services.
also: actor
cybercrime group concept
A cybercrime group is an organized group that uses computers or the internet to commit crimes.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
cybersecurity experts organization
Cybersecurity experts are people who specialize in protecting computers, networks, and data from attacks.
cybersecurity firms concept
Companies that provide services and products to protect organizations from digital threats.
Danfoss organization
Danfoss is a company that makes industrial, heating, cooling, and refrigeration-control equipment.
dark web leak site concept
A dark web leak site is a hidden website where criminals publish stolen data to pressure victims or advertise breaches.
also: leak site
dark web marketplaces concept
Online hidden shops on darknets like Tor that sell illegal goods and services, including stolen data, malware, and drugs.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
also: cybersecurity incident, data security incident, data breaches
data encryption concept
Data encryption is the process of transforming data so it cannot be read without the right key.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
also: steal data
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
Data Prioritization concept
The process of deciding which data is most important to protect, use, or address first.
data stores concept
Places where digital information is kept, such as databases, file systems, or cloud storage services.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
Data transfers concept
Data transfers are movements of information from one person, system, company, or country to another.
Database product
A database is an organized collection of data that software can store, search, and update.
Database Configuration concept
The settings that control how a database operates, connects to services, and protects its data.
Database credentials concept
Database credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens used to access a database.
Dates of birth concept
Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.
DebugBear organization
A website-performance monitoring service that helps organizations measure and improve website speed and user experience.
deception technique
Deception is tricking a person or system into believing something false, often to gain access or hide activity.
Decrypt technique
Decrypt is a cryptographic operation that turns encrypted data back into readable data when the correct key is used.
Decryption Keys concept
Decryption keys are secret pieces of information used to turn encrypted data back into readable data.
default credentials concept
Default credentials are factory-set usernames and passwords that should be changed because attackers often know them.
Default passwords concept
Default passwords are factory-set passwords that should be changed because attackers often know them.
Defend concept
Defend means to protect systems, networks, data, or users from cyber threats.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
defense-sector other
The segment of government and industry focused on military, national security, and critical infrastructure protection.
defensive cyber capabilities concept
Defensive cyber capabilities are tools, skills, and processes used to protect systems, detect attacks, and respond to incidents.
DeFi concept
DeFi, short for decentralized finance, refers to financial services built on blockchains rather than run by a traditional bank.
also: DeFi companies
Defrost mode concept
A refrigeration operating mode that temporarily melts frost or ice from cooling equipment.
Defused Cyber organization
Defused Cyber is a cybersecurity organization or service name associated with cyber threat intelligence and security research.
Delegation concept
Delegation is the act of giving another account, service, or smart contract permission to perform actions on one's behalf.
deleted concept
Deleted means removed from normal access, though copies may sometimes still exist in backups, logs, or recovery areas.
Delhaize organization
A Belgian supermarket and retail brand owned by Ahold Delhaize.
Dependabot tool
A GitHub tool that automatically monitors dependencies and opens pull requests to fix vulnerable packages.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components that a project relies on to work.
dependency concept
A dependency is outside software that an application relies on, which can create risk if that outside component is vulnerable or malicious.
Deposits and Withdrawals concept
Transactions that add money to or remove money from an account or financial platform.
Designated Service Account concept
A specific nonhuman cloud account created for a limited, authorized purpose.
Detect technique
Detect means to identify suspicious or malicious activity in systems, networks, or data.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
detection engineering technique
Detection engineering is the work of creating, testing, and improving rules or logic that spot suspicious activity in systems.
detection rules concept
Detection rules are instructions security tools use to flag suspicious behavior or known attack patterns.
detections concept
Alerts or findings generated by security tools indicating that a potential threat or malicious activity has been identified.
deterministic concept
A system or function that always produces the same output for the same input, with no random variation.
Dev Machine Guard tool
Dev Machine Guard is a security tool or product name referenced in reporting.
Developer Device concept
A computer used by a software developer to write, test, or manage code.
Developer Endpoints concept
Developer endpoints are the laptops, desktops, or other devices used by people who create software.
Developer Infrastructure concept
Developer infrastructure is the collection of systems and services used to build, store, test, and release software.
Developer machines concept
Developer machines are computers used by software developers to write, build, and test code.
DevOps engineer concept
A technology professional who helps build, run, automate, and maintain an organization's software systems.
digital assets concept
Digital assets are valuable items that exist electronically, such as cryptocurrency, tokens, files, or online accounts.
digital signage devices product
Electronic displays used to show advertisements, notices, menus, or other information.
DigitalOcean organization
DigitalOcean is a cloud provider that offers virtual servers, storage, and developer infrastructure.
direct internet access concept
Direct internet access means a system can connect to or be reached from the internet without going through extra protective layers.
DirectAdmin product
A web-based control panel used to manage web-hosting servers, websites, email, and databases.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
DiskStation Manager product
Synology's operating system for its network-attached storage devices.
DiskStation Manager (DSM) product
Synology's operating system for its network-attached storage devices.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
DIVD organization
DIVD, the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, is a Dutch nonprofit organization that helps identify and report security flaws.
also: the non-profit cybersecurity organization DIVD
DKIM protocol
DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.
DLL sideloading technique
DLL sideloading is an attack where malware places a fake DLL where a trusted Windows program will load it.
also: a DLL sideloading chain
docker
Docker is a platform for packaging and running applications in containers.
Domain Administrator Accounts concept
Highly privileged accounts that can control computers and users across a Windows domain.
also: backdoor domain administrator accounts
downloader malware
A downloader is malware or a small program that retrieves and installs additional malicious code from the internet.
Drift product
Drift is a customer messaging and marketing platform used by businesses to chat with website visitors and manage sales conversations.
Dropbox product
Dropbox is a cloud storage and file-sharing service.
droppers malware
Droppers are malware programs whose main job is to install or download other malware onto a device.
also: single-stage droppers
dual-use concept
Dual-use means something can be used for helpful defensive purposes or for harmful offensive purposes.
dual-use tools concept
Tools that can be used for legitimate purposes but can also be misused for harmful activity.
Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure organization
A Dutch organization involved in identifying and responsibly reporting security vulnerabilities.
Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) organization
The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, or DIVD, is a Dutch nonprofit organization that helps identify and report security flaws.
eCh0raix malware
A ransomware family, also known as QNAPCrypt, that encrypts files on targeted network storage devices.
Ed25519 protocol
Ed25519 is a modern digital-signature algorithm used to prove data or messages came from the expected sender and were not changed.
editor and admin API protocol
An application programming interface used to manage and configure an application's editor and administrative features.
egress concept
Egress is outbound traffic or data leaving a network, system, or cloud environment.
EIP-7702 protocol
EIP-7702 is an Ethereum proposal that lets a regular account temporarily delegate actions to smart-contract code.
EIP-7702 authorization mechanism protocol
An Ethereum proposal that lets an account authorize code to act on its behalf under specified conditions.
Election Record concept
The collection of ballot and election data used to verify and calculate an election result.
also: published election record
election security concept
Election security means protecting voting systems, election data, and related processes from tampering, disruption, or misinformation.
ElectionGuard product
A cryptographic election system from Microsoft that adds verifiable voting features to election processes.
Electronic Ballot Return concept
Submitting a completed ballot electronically, such as by internet, email, or fax.
also: online voting, internet voting
Elliptic organization
Elliptic is a company that analyzes cryptocurrency transactions to help detect fraud, sanctions evasion, and money laundering.
email addresses concept
Email addresses are the unique names people use to send and receive email, such as user@example.com.
Email Bombing technique
Sending a very large number of emails to overwhelm a person or mailbox.
Email security concept
Email security protects inboxes and users from threats such as phishing, malware, and scam messages.
email security gateway product
An email security gateway is a system that scans email before it reaches a recipient’s mailbox.
Employee credentials concept
Employee credentials are usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login details used by workers.
Employee’s Computer concept
A computer assigned to or used by a worker.
encoding concept
Encoding is changing data into a particular format so computers can store, send, or interpret it.
Encrypt technique
Encrypt is the process of turning readable data into scrambled data that only someone with the right key can read.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
also: keys that protect it
encrypted payload concept
Hidden code or data that must be decrypted before it can run or be used.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
Encryption keys concept
Encryption keys are secret values used to lock and unlock protected data.
end of life concept
The point when a vendor stops supporting a product, including no longer providing security fixes.
end to end concept
End to end means something is handled across the whole process from start to finish, often without gaps between steps.
end-of-life systems concept
Computers or software that are no longer supported by their maker and therefore no longer receive normal security updates.
End-to-End Verifiability concept
An election property that lets voters and the public check that votes were included and counted correctly.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
endpoint protection concept
Endpoint protection is security software or controls used to protect devices like laptops, phones, and servers from malware and other attacks.
Endpoint Protections concept
Security tools installed on devices such as computers and phones to detect, block, or investigate attacks.
endpoint scanning technique
Endpoint scanning is checking laptops, servers, phones, or other devices for vulnerabilities, malware, or risky settings.
endpoint security concept
Endpoint security is protection for user devices such as laptops, desktops, and phones.
endpoint security protection tools tool
Security software on computers and other devices that tries to detect, block, or investigate threats.
also: endpoint security tools
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.
energy concept
Energy is the sector that produces and delivers electricity, fuel, and related services.
engagement concept
Engagement means how often people interact with a website, app, message, or notification.
Enrich technique
Enrich means adding useful context, such as user or location details, to security data.
enterprise authentication concept
The process of verifying the identities of employees and users in a business's systems.
enterprise LLM product
An enterprise LLM is a large language model service or deployment intended for business use, often with added security, privacy, and management controls.
entry point concept
An entry point is the place or method an attacker, program, or process first uses to get into a system or workflow.
EPSS concept
EPSS is a scoring system that estimates how likely a software vulnerability is to be exploited in the real world.
escaping technique
Escaping means changing special characters in text so a computer treats them as normal text instead of as commands or code.
eset
ESET is a cybersecurity company that makes antivirus, endpoint protection, and threat research products.
espionage concept
Espionage is spying to gather information without permission.
ethereum
Ethereum is a blockchain platform used for cryptocurrency, smart contracts, and decentralized applications.
Eurojust organization
Eurojust is the European Union agency that helps countries cooperate on criminal justice investigations.
europe
Europe is a continent often referenced in cybersecurity reporting involving regulations, victims, threat activity, or law enforcement.
European authorities organization
European authorities refers to government or law-enforcement agencies in Europe involved in investigations or enforcement actions.
European law enforcement organization
European law enforcement refers to police or investigative agencies in Europe that investigate and disrupt criminal activity.
European Parliament organization
The European Parliament is the elected law-making body of the European Union and can investigate or regulate issues such as spyware and digital rights.
European Summit other
European Summit is a named event or meeting in Europe referenced in reporting.

public records concept

pyproject.toml concept

query parameter concept

ransom concept

Reasoning concept

Red Hat Enterprise Linux product

repository concept

researchers organization

robotics concept
